requirement.evidence: It shall be unlawful and a violation of the “New Jersey Antitrust Act,” P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a.     a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
requirement.note: Card paraphrases sections 4, 3 and 7 accurately: ban on using coordinators, parallel pricing coordination, AG complaint location. Minor simplification of 'coordinating function' definition, which also covers a landlord's own use.

key_value.evidence: b.    a coordinator to facilitate a tacit or express agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function;
key_value.note: Ban on providing/using coordination services and designation as an Antitrust Act violation are stated.

effective_date.evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
effective_date.note: Approval date July 20, 2026 is stated; the computation to 2027-07-01 is a small step the card explains. The document does not state the calendar date itself.

status.evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
status.note: As of 2026-10-01 the act, approved July 20, 2026, has not yet taken effect, so not_yet_effective follows from the text.

coverage.note: Card coverage is null; the document lists no unit thresholds or construction cutoffs.

citation.note: The document supports P.L. 2026, c.43 and the C.56:9-20 to 56:9-26 codification range for sections 1-7. The 'N.J.S.A.' prefix and the A3497 ACS 1R reference are consistent with the header, but sections 8-9 are not within that range.
